title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: The Mathematics Department's course on ordinary differential equations: classification and formation of ODEs, first-order methods, second- and nth-order linear equations, undetermined coefficients and variation of parameters, the operator D method, difference equations, and numerical interpolation and integration. Built from A. O. Akeju's class slides (Chapters 1 to 4, Lecture 5, the operator D, difference equation and numerical integration slides), H. O. Tejumola's DLC text and the past papers from 2011/12 to 2014/15.

topics.title: Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations
topics.summary: An ODE relates an unknown function of one independent variable to its derivatives. ODEs are classified by order, degree and linearity; their solutions are general or particular, fixed by initial conditions in an initial value problem. ODEs are formed by eliminating arbitrary constants and arise in growth, decay and cooling problems.
subtopics: What an ODE is; ODEs versus PDEs

topics.title: First-Order Differential Equations
topics.summary: First-order equations are solved by type: separable, homogeneous (with y = vx), exact (when ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x), linear (with an integrating factor) and Bernoulli (reduced to linear). Non-exact equations can sometimes be made exact with an integrating factor.
subtopics: Exact equations and the test for exactness

topics.title: Higher-Order Linear Homogeneous Equations
topics.summary: Linear homogeneous equations with constant coefficients are solved through the auxiliary (characteristic) equation. Distinct real roots give exponentials, repeated roots add powers of x, and complex roots a ± ib give e^(ax)(A cos bx + B sin bx). The general solution of a linear equation is a combination of n independent solutions.

topics.title: Undetermined Coefficients and Variation of Parameters
topics.summary: For a non-homogeneous linear equation, a particular integral is found by the method of undetermined coefficients, guessing a form like the right-hand side, or by variation of parameters, which replaces the constants of the complementary function by functions found from a Wronskian. Initial conditions then fix the constants.
subtopics: Undetermined coefficients: choosing the trial form
Modification when the trial form is in the complementary function

topics.title: The Operator D Method
topics.summary: Writing D = d/dx turns a linear equation with constant coefficients into f(D)y = g(x). The complementary function comes from f(m) = 0, and particular integrals come from inverse operators 1/f(D) with rules for exponentials, sines and cosines, polynomials and exponential shifts, or by reduction of order through partial fractions.
subtopics: The operator D and f(D)y = g(x)
1/f(D²) applied to sin ax and cos ax
Reduction of order and partial fractions

topics.title: Difference Equations
topics.summary: Finite differences measure changes in tabulated values: forward differences Δ, backward differences ∇ and the shift operator E. A difference equation relates successive terms y_n; it is formed by eliminating constants and solved, when linear with constant coefficients, through its characteristic equation plus a particular solution.

topics.title: Numerical Interpolation and Integration
topics.summary: Numerical methods approximate functions and integrals from tabulated values. Lagrange and Newton interpolation fit polynomials through data points, numerical differentiation uses finite differences, and quadrature rules from the Newton-Cotes formula, the trapezoidal rule and Simpson's 1/3 rule, approximate definite integrals with known error bounds.
